{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Convert revenue from string to float, removing commas
# First, check for the QA rows: revenue = 999999.99
daemon_rows = df[df['revenue'] == '999999.99']
print(f'Number of QA rows (revenue = 999999.99): {daemon_rows.shape[0]}')

# Convert revenue to float after removing commas
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Check if any QA rows are present
print(f'QA rows in dataset? {daemon_rows.shape[0] > 0}')

# Now drop QA rows
df_clean = df[~((df['revenue'] == '999999.99') | (df['revenue'] == '999999.99'))]

# Also drop refunded orders — per contract, population is only completed
df_clean = df_clean[df_clean['status'] == 'completed']

# Check final population size
print(f'Final population size (completed orders, no QA): {df_clean.shape[0]}')

# Now compute conversion rate by customer_segment
# Since converted is already 1 or 0, and we're only looking at completed orders,
# the conversion rate is just the mean of converted within each segment
conversion_rate_by_segment = df_clean.groupby('customer_segment', observed=True)['converted'].mean()
print(conversion_rate_by_segment)

# Find the segment with highest conversion rate
best_segment = conversion_rate_by_segment.idxmax()
print(f'Highest conversion rate segment: {best_segment}')"}
